title: Tic-Tac-Toe Redux
mechanic: Typed game state and a game loop

scenario.title: A game state you can trust
scenario.body: This program asks questions instead of taking arguments, so the book has no command-line tests for it, only checks of the board drawing and the winner. These tests play real games: one move at a time through get_move(), whole games typed in at the keyboard, and hundreds of made-up move lists from Hypothesis. A natural first version keeps one game object and changes it with each move. That version calls a ninth-move win a draw, lets O move after X has won, and crashes when the keyboard runs out.

note: The book doesn't give this chapter any command-line tests, because the program asks for moves while it runs. Here a whole game is typed in at once by sending the moves through STDIN, one per line.

character.name: Tic and Tac
character.role: two tiger cubs who never stop playing

tagline: Play a whole game of noughts and crosses against a friend (or yourself). Tic and Tac keep score and shout when somebody wins.

brain_blurbs.book: Keeps one game and scribbles every move onto it.
brain_blurbs.real: Makes a fresh copy of the game for every move, and checks for a win first.

rules.test_board_no_state: Draws an empty board numbered 1 to 9
rules.test_board_with_state: Draws X and O where they've been played
rules.test_winning: Spots every way to win: rows, columns and diagonals
rules.test_losing: Doesn't call a winner too early
rules.test_new_game_is_empty: A new game is empty and X goes first
rules.test_players_take_turns: X, then O, then X again
rules.test_taken_cell_is_an_error: No playing on a square that's taken (and it's still your turn)
rules.test_a_win: Three X's across the top: X wins!
rules.test_ninth_move_win_is_a_win_not_a_draw: Winning with the very last square is a win, not a draw
rules.test_a_real_draw: A full board with no winner is a draw
rules.test_no_moves_after_the_game_is_won: Once someone has won, no more sneaky moves
rules.test_old_state_is_never_changed: Every move makes a new copy of the game; the old one never changes
rules.test_whole_game_at_the_keyboard: A whole game typed in ends with "X has won!"
rules.test_keyboard_runs_out_of_moves: If the moves stop early, it says bye instead of crashing
rules.test_turns_stay_fair: Whatever anyone types, X never gets two turns in a row
rules.test_each_move_fills_at_most_one_square: A move fills one empty square, or none, and never rubs one out
rules.test_never_two_winners: X and O can never both win
rules.test_draw_means_full_and_no_winner: A draw only happens when the board is full and nobody won
rules.test_game_over_means_nothing_changes: When the game is over, more typing changes nothing
